isabel-support: Heads-up — customer acme-finance says CloudTrail has NO KmsEncrypt/KmsDecrypt events for a 15m window around their key rotation (2025-07-10T02:00:00Z -> 02:15:00Z). They rotated an AWS KMS key via our proxy and then saw successful Decrypt responses but nothing in CloudTrail. Also reported a billing spike. @emily-security fyi
raj-dev: Ack. Do we have any request IDs or SDK logs from the customer? That will help map to CloudTrail RequestId fields.
isabel-support: Pasted the stripped logs they sent (sanitized):
```
2025-07-10T02:01:12Z INFO KMS-CLIENT req=0a1b2c3d4 Decrypt called encryptionContext={"user":"acme-prod"} requestId=req-0a1b2c3d
2025-07-10T02:01:13Z INFO PROXY forward req=req-0a1b2c3d upstreamReqId=up-99aaee
2025-07-10T02:01:13Z INFO KMS-CLIENT resp=0a1b2c3d status=200 kmsRequestId=abcd-1234-efgh
```

isabel-support: They say CloudTrail shows no event with kmsRequestId abcd-1234-efgh and no KmsDecrypt entries in that timeframe.
emily-security: Hmm — possible places to lose audit events: 1) CloudTrail event selectors (management vs data events), 2) proxy mutating/removing fields so event filtering doesn't match, 3) CloudTrail ingestion delay/retention rules, 4) cross-account KMS calls where events go to a different trail. Did the customer have a cross-account setup?
isabel-support: They said same account, but using our on-prem HSM proxy for private deployment. The proxy forwards to AWS KMS for a subset of operations.
dave-infra: Checking proxy logs now. Quick grep shows some drops around 02:01:13. Snippet:
```
2025-07-10T02:01:12.998 proxy-01 WARN drop_meta: request up-99aaee missing header X-EncCtx
2025-07-10T02:01:13.002 proxy-02 INFO forwarded up-99aaee -> abcd-1234
2025-07-10T02:01:13.100 proxy-03 ERROR transient_conn: tls handshake timeout, queued->fallback
```

raj-dev: If the proxy strips a custom header we use to reconstruct encryptionContext in CloudTrail (we sometimes add an x-amz-meta header for audit), CloudTrail won't show the context but the KMS management event should still exist. Are you certain there are NO KmsDecrypt entries at all? Have they checked both the management events and the KMS data events?
isabel-support: Customer looked in CloudTrail Console -> Event history and also S3 bucket where trail delivers logs. They say both have no KmsDecrypt entries for that key id between 02:00-02:15.
oncall-ml: Billing spike: could be from fallback to hosted KMS endpoints or retries. If proxy had transient TLS error proxy-03 showed, some traffic might have rerouted to a different backend that is metered differently. Worth correlating request counts.
emily-security: Next steps: get full request IDs (upstream & kmsRequestId), CloudTrail query for that time window, and proxy node logs for all three nodes. Also check CloudTrail event selectors and S3 object lifecycle (maybe logs were delivered then expired by aggressive lifecycle?). Run:
```
aws cloudtrail get-event-selectors --trail-name MyTrail
aws s3 ls s3://my-trail-bucket/ --recursive --start-after "2025/07/10/02/00"
```

raj-dev: To reproduce locally against our proxy:
1) Start proxy in dev mode (set PROXY_DROP_METADATA=true)
2) Run curl to KMS shim:
```
curl -v -H "X-Amz-Target: TrentService.Decrypt" -H "Content-Type: application/x-amz-json-1.1" \
  -H "X-EncCtx: {\"user\":\"acme-prod\"}" \
  --data-binary '{"CiphertextBlob":"...base64..."}' http://localhost:8080/
```
Expected: proxy forwards header to AWS KMS as encryptionContext. If PROXY_DROP_METADATA=true, header removed and CloudTrail might still show event but not context.
isabel-support: Customer also provided S3 object list; bucket showed an object for 02:02:00 but the delivered CloudTrail file is only management plane events, no KmsDecrypt entries. I can share the object name.
emily-security: Also check whether the trail is multi-region and if the KMS calls were to a regional key — events may land in a different region's trail. Run CloudTrail lookup: `aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=Decrypt --start-time 2025-07-10T01:50:00Z --end-time 2025-07-10T02:20:00Z`
dave-infra: I grep'd proxy storage and found a race where a queued request that hit tls timeout was retried directly to AWS KMS via a different host that uses a different IAM role, which could send events to another account's trail in cross-account setups. Adding that to the list.
